our-lady.index.title: Our Lady of Kibeho
our-lady.index.subtitle: Nyina wa Jambo — Mother of the Word
our-lady.index.intro:
Kibeho is a remote site in Nyaruguru District, in the Southern Province of Rwanda. It is about a three-hour drive from Kigali and about 30 kilometres from Huye. The apparitions of the Virgin Mary have made Kibeho a place of prayer and pilgrimage.

Here seekers of God come to ask for the grace of conversion, to offer their intentions in reparation, and to promote reconciliation between persons, communities, and nations.

our-lady.apparitions.title: The Apparitions
our-lady.apparitions.subtitle: 28 November 1981 – 28 November 1989
our-lady.apparitions.intro:
The first time the Virgin Mary appeared to Alphonsine Mumureke, a student in the school now called Groupe Scolaire Mère du Verbe Kibeho, was on 28 November 1981, in a dining hall. Alphonsine saw a beautiful woman who presented herself as Nyina wa Jambo — Mother of the Word.

On 12 January 1982 the Blessed Virgin appeared to Nathalie Mukamazimpaka in the dormitory, and on 2 March 1982 to Marie Claire Mukangango. Others reported visions, but only these three visionaries were approved by the Church in 2001 after a thorough investigation.

blocks.text: Where the apparitions took place

From 28 November 1981 to May 1982, the apparitions took place in the dormitory, later transformed into the Chapel of the Apparitions. From 31 May 1982 to 28 November 1989 they were held outside the dormitory; from 15 August 1982 a long part of them took place at the podium.

items: Marie Claire Mukangango — 2 March 1982 to 15 September 1982

our-lady.visionaries.title: The Visionaries
our-lady.visionaries.subtitle: The three recognised visionaries of Kibeho
our-lady.visionaries.intro: The Church recognised the authenticity of the apparitions associated with three students of Kibeho. Through them the Mother of the Word called the world to faith, conversion, and prayer.

items.title: Alphonsine Mumureke
items.text: The first visionary. Apparitions began on 28 November 1981 in the school dining hall. She received the Virgin Mary until 28 November 1989.

items.title: Nathalie Mukamazimpaka
items.text: The Virgin Mary appeared to her on 12 January 1982 in the dormitory. Her apparitions continued until 3 December 1983. She was called to prayer, penance, and redemptive suffering.

items.title: Marie Claire Mukangango
items.text: Apparitions from 2 March 1982 to 15 September 1982. She is especially linked with the devotion of the Rosary of the Seven Sorrows.

our-lady.messages.title: The Messages
our-lady.messages.subtitle: Faith, conversion, and prayer
our-lady.messages.intro:
Faith, conversion, and prayer were the heart of the Virgin Mary’s messages to the three girls — and through them to the whole world. She presented herself as a Mother calling her children: Mwana (Child) and Ndi Nyina wa Jambo (I am the Mother of the Word).

She said the world conducts itself very badly, hastens to its ruin, and is rebellious against God. “If you do not repent and do not convert your hearts, you will fall into the abyss.” This is a call to conversion and reconciliation.

items: Convert while there is still time
Pray the Rosary, especially the Seven Sorrows Rosary
Offer reparation for your sins and the sins of the world
Seek reconciliation between persons, communities, and nations
Live as children of the Mother of the Word

blocks.text: The first words at Kibeho remain fundamental: she is a Mother calling all her children — Mother of the Church (cf. Jn 19:27) and Mother of God (Council of Ephesus, 431).

our-lady.church-recognition.title: Church Recognition
our-lady.church-recognition.subtitle: Declared authentic on 29 June 2001
our-lady.church-recognition.intro:
After the supernatural events, some remained in doubt while others waited for the judgement of the Church. The investigations concluded by recognising the apparitions of Kibeho as authentic.

On 29 June 2001, after the approval of the Holy See, the Bishop of Gikongoro, Mgr Augustin Misago, issued the declaration bearing the final judgement on the apparitions of Kibeho. Bishop Jean Baptiste Gahamanyi had earlier created two commissions: medical (March 1982) and theological (May 1982).

Marian apparitions have been reported throughout the world; the Church has recognised a number of them, such as Guadalupe, Fatima, and Lourdes. Kibeho is among them — the first approved on the African continent.

our-lady.history.title: History
our-lady.history.subtitle: Before, during, and after the apparitions
our-lady.history.intro: Kibeho Sanctuary stands in a parish erected in 1934, born from Kansi Parish (1910), itself born from Save, the oldest parish in Rwanda. The parish was dedicated to the Mother of God (Umubyeyi w’Imana) and was known for strong Christian life and many vocations.

blocks.text: Before

Kibeho College, where the apparitions happened, was founded in 1968 and entrusted to the Benebikira Sisters, who still serve there. It was a simple school like many others in Rwanda until 28 November 1981.
During

From 1981 to 1989 the history of Kibeho changed. To Alphonsine the Virgin Mary said “Ndi Nyina wa Jambo” — “I am the Mother of the Word.” People from every corner of Rwanda and from abroad began to come. Newspapers such as Kinyamateka and Imvaho, and radio, spoke of what was happening. Why Kibeho? The Virgin Mary said she appears to whom she wants and when she wants.

Bishop Jean Baptiste Gahamanyi created two commissions: a medical commission in March 1982 and a theological commission in May 1982. The three recognised visionaries — Alphonsine Mumureke (28 November 1981 – 28 November 1989), Nathalie Mukamazimpaka (12 January 1982 – 3 December 1983), and Marie Claire Mukangango (2 March 1982 – 15 September 1982) — helped the Church understand and spread the message.
After

On 29 June 2001, after the approval of the Holy See, Bishop Augustin Misago of Gikongoro issued the declaration recognising the apparitions of Kibeho as authentic. Among Marian apparitions approved by the Church — such as Guadalupe, Lourdes, and Fatima — Kibeho is the first approved on the African continent.

items.title: Are the apparitions recognised?
items.text: Yes. On 29 June 2001 the Bishop of Gikongoro declared authentic the apparitions to Alphonsine Mumureke, Nathalie Mukamazimpaka, and Marie Claire Mukangango.

items.title: Where is Kibeho?
items.text: In Nyaruguru District, Southern Province, Rwanda, in the Diocese of Gikongoro, not far from the border with Burundi. It is about three hours from Kigali and about 30 km from Huye.

items.title: How do I plan a visit?
items.text: Contact the Pilgrimage Office. Foreign pilgrims may also be helped by the St. Vincent Pallotti Pilgrimages Centre in Kigali.

shrine.index.title: The Shrine
shrine.index.subtitle: A living place of prayer on the hills of Kibeho
shrine.index.intro: The Shrine of Our Lady of Kibeho welcomes pilgrims who come to pray, to celebrate the sacraments, and to walk the places linked to the apparitions of the Mother of the Word. Here the Church gathers each day — and, on feast days, from across Rwanda and the world.

blocks.text: Life of prayer

Holy Mass, the Rosary, confession, and times of silence shape the ordinary day at the Shrine. On Marian feasts and major pilgrimages the liturgy is extended, and the grounds fill with parishes, dioceses, and visitors from many nations.
Places to visit

Begin with a welcome and orientation, then move through the churches, apparition sites, Holy Spring, and Way of the Cross at a prayerful pace. The Mass schedule and shrine map will help you plan the day.

The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Kibeho welcomes pilgrims from Rwanda and around the world. Come to pray, to celebrate the sacraments, and to encounter the Mother of the Word.

Kibeho is a holy place with the Church of Our Lady of Sorrows, the Chapel of the Apparitions, the Chapel of Adoration, the Way of the Cross, the Way of the Rosary, the source of Mary, and other places of prayer.

pilgrimage.why-kibeho.title: Why Kibeho?
pilgrimage.why-kibeho.subtitle: A recognised Marian shrine in Africa
pilgrimage.why-kibeho.intro:
The Apparitions of the Virgin Mary have made Kibeho a place of prayer and pilgrimage. Kibeho is a place of prayer for seekers of God who come to ask for the grace of conversion, offering their intentions in reparation for their own sins and the sins of the world, and to promote reconciliation between individuals, communities, and nations.

It is the first Marian apparition site on the African continent approved by the Catholic Church.

pilgrimage.plan.title: Plan your Pilgrimage
pilgrimage.plan.subtitle: Prepare your journey to the Sanctuary
pilgrimage.plan.intro:
Whether you come alone, with family, or with a parish group, the Sanctuary welcomes you. Follow the path on this page, then write to the Pilgrimage Office so liturgy, lodging, and a fitting welcome can be prepared.

Pilgrims from abroad can fly to Kigali. From Kigali, the St. Vincent Pallotti Pilgrimages Centre can help you find facilities for your pilgrimage to Kibeho.

blocks.text: A simple path

items.title: Who is coming?
items.text: One person, a family, or a parish group. Note languages spoken and whether you need a priest or a local guide.

items.title: When will you come?
items.text: Ordinary days are quieter. Marian feasts and national pilgrimages are crowded — confirm dates on the calendar before you book travel.

items.title: How will you arrive?
items.text: International pilgrims fly to Kigali (about three hours by road). Usual routes include Kigali–Huye–Matyazo–Kibeho.

pilgrimage.transportation.subtitle: How to reach the Sanctuary
pilgrimage.transportation.intro:
The Sanctuary Our Lady of Kibeho is situated in the Diocese of Gikongoro, Nyaruguru District, in Southern Rwanda, not far from the Burundian border. It is about a three-hour drive from Kigali and about 30 kilometres from Huye.

Pilgrims from foreign countries can use the airplane that lands in Kigali, the capital city of Rwanda. From Kigali, the St. Vincent Pallotti Pilgrimages Centre can help you find facilities for your pilgrimage.

spirituality.seven-sorrows-rosary.title: Seven Sorrows Rosary
spirituality.seven-sorrows-rosary.subtitle: The distinctive devotion of Kibeho
spirituality.seven-sorrows-rosary.intro: Our Lady asked, especially through Marie Claire Mukangango, that the faithful pray the Rosary of the Seven Sorrows — meditating on the sorrows of Mary and uniting our hearts to her Son. This is the prayer most closely bound to Kibeho.

blocks.text: How to pray
Begin with an Act of Contrition. For each sorrow: one Our Father and seven Hail Marys, with a brief meditation on that mystery. End with three Hail Marys in honour of the tears of Our Lady.
The seven sorrows

items: The Loss of the Child Jesus in the Temple
Mary meets Jesus on the Way of the Cross
Mary receives the Body of Jesus

blocks.text: Pray it at home if you cannot yet come. When you do come, you may walk the Way of the Cross on the hillside after Mass.

support.index.title: Support the Shrine
support.index.subtitle: Prayer and material support
support.index.intro:
Until now, the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Kibeho is constituted by the church of Our Lady of Sorrows, the Chapel of the Apparitions, the place and esplanade of the apparitions, the Way of the Rosary, the Way of the Rosary of the Seven Sorrows, the Way of the Cross, the chapel of adoration, the source of Mary, and a shop of devotional items.

Other projects are planned for a better welcome and a better service towards pilgrims. We are all invited to contribute, through prayer and material support, so that Kibeho may truly become the place of conversion and reconciliation that the Mother of God has appealed for.
